label: TsBuckBoost
info:
Two things:

1. A switch that shows the individual Buck-Boost temperatures as separate
   Venus devices, or hides them again.
2. Four inputs that read those temperatures straight from the converter's
   own service - these work whether the switch is on or off.

IMPORTANT: the switch writes the settings value
/Settings/Devices/tsbuckboost/SeparateTempSensors on
com.victronenergy.settings - NOT the converter's /Mode path.
/Mode is the pin 1 mirror and is written by the driver every 2 seconds.

Switching restarts the driver and then the GX user interface, so the device
list is redrawn. The display goes black for a few seconds; nothing else on
the system is affected.

name: TsBuckBoost: show temperatures as separate devices
info:
Setting: /Settings/Devices/tsbuckboost/SeparateTempSensors
1 = on, 0 = off. The value survives reboots and package updates.

The flow reads the setting before writing and only acts on a real change,
and it ignores whatever arrives in the first five seconds after a deploy -
the virtual switch emits its state then, which is not a command.
On a real change the driver is restarted, then the GX user interface, so
the device list is redrawn.

The temperatures themselves are always on D-Bus in the converter's own
service - see the four input nodes below. The switch only decides whether
Venus also lists them as devices of their own.

name: build settings command
result
Temperatures straight from the converter - no extra devices needed
info:
These read the paths the driver always publishes on its own service,
whether the separate temperature devices are switched on or not.

If the nodes show no service, open one and pick the Buck-Boost from
the list, then type the path by hand. The service is stored as
com.victronenergy.alternator.<device instance>; 40 is the default of
the driver, yours may differ - check with:
  dbus -y com.victronenergy.settings \
       /Settings/Devices/tsbuckboost/ClassAndVrmInstance GetValue
